statement: Let H be the set of depths d ≥ 0 for which root has at least one node at depth d (the root, when present, has depth 0; a child of a depth-d node has depth d+1). For nodes at the same depth, order them left-to-right by their root-to-node paths, where at the first differing step a left-child step is before a right-child step. Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) = |H|, and for every d with 0 ≤ d < len(r), r[d] is the value of the unique node at depth d that is rightmost at that depth, i.e. no node at depth d is to the right of it.
preconditions: root is a Tree with at most 100 Node constructors, and every node value v satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: For every root satisfying the preconditions, right_side_view returns a result r and does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow).
preconditions: root is a Tree with at most 100 Node constructors, and every node value v satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of nonnegative depths d at which root has at least one node. Equivalently, if root is Null then len(r) = 0, and if root is not Null then len(r) = 1 + max{d ≥ 0 | root has a node at depth d}, where depth 0 is the root.
preconditions: root is a Tree with at most 100 Node constructors, and every node value v satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) ≥ 1 and r[0] is the value stored at the root node of root.
preconditions: root is not Null, root has at most 100 nodes, and every node value in root satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(r), there exists a node n at depth i of root such that the value of n is r[i] and no node at depth i of root is strictly to the right of n. Nodes at the same depth are ordered left-to-right by their root-to-node paths: at the first step where two paths differ, a left-child step is to the left of a right-child step.
preconditions: root is a Tree with at most 100 Node constructors, and every node value v satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(r), -100 ≤ r[i] ≤ 100.
preconditions: root is a Tree with at most 100 Node constructors, and every node value v satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) is at most the number of Node constructors in root; in particular len(r) ≤ 100.
preconditions: root is a Tree with at most 100 Node constructors, and every node value v satisfies -100 ≤ v ≤ 100.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) ≥ 2, and r[1] = w, the value stored at the root of the right subtree of root.
preconditions: root = Node(v, L, Node(w, A, B)) for some value v, value w, and trees L, A, B; all node values are in [-100,100] and root has at most 100 nodes.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) ≥ 2 and r[1] = w, the value stored at the root of the left subtree of root.
preconditions: root = Node(v, Node(w, A, B), Null) for some value v, value w, and trees A, B; all node values are in [-100,100] and root has at most 100 nodes.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) equals the number of nodes in root, and for every i with 0 ≤ i < len(r), r[i] is the value of the unique node at depth i in root. Thus r lists the values along the unique root-to-leaf path from top to bottom, and r is empty when root is Null.
preconditions: Every node in root has at most one non-Null child (so root is either Null or a single downward path); every node value is in [-100,100]; root has at most 100 nodes.

statement: Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, for every depth d ≥ 1 with d < len(r), consider depth d-1 measured from the root of a subtree. If R has at least one node at depth d-1, then r[d] is the value of the rightmost node at depth d-1 in R, using the same left-to-right path order inside R; otherwise L has at least one node at depth d-1 and r[d] is the value of the rightmost node at depth d-1 in L.
preconditions: root = Node(v, L, R) for some value v and trees L, R; every node value is in [-100,100]; root has at most 100 nodes.

statement: Let h be the height of the nonempty perfect tree root. Whenever right_side_view returns a result r, len(r) = h+1, and for every d with 0 ≤ d ≤ h, r[d] is the value of the node reached from the root by taking the right child exactly d times.
preconditions: root is a nonempty perfect binary tree of height h for some h ≥ 0: root is not Null, every node at depth < h has two non-Null children, every node at depth h is a leaf, and there are no nodes at depth > h. Every node value is in [-100,100], and root has at most 100 nodes.
